questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The department of applied Physics. They have a great department for solid state physics and courses in mesoscopic physics that I really wanted to get deeper into. Then the aspect of applied physics also sounded great since I have always done very theoretical physics.

questions.answer: Great. I had all the help I need and the staff is great at helping if you ask.

questions.answer: DUWO is great.

questions.answer: No meal plans but kitchens in all apartments I feel.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Sign up early for DUWO. I would have preferred to live at prof S

Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great. You can sign up for multiple courses, go to lectures the first few weeks and then decide later which to follow. You basically just sign up for the exams.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Online at my.tudelft

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Just ask the student councilors they can help with everything

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont stress about it

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: High level. It was great but required a lot of work. Some classes especially are tough and require you to both study well but also to get really good at problem solving.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Lectures, exercise classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Advanced statistical mechanics
- Physics of energy materials
- Mesoscopic physics
- Scientific computing
- Introduction to Financial Mathematics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Advanced statistical mechanics is tough but so great and satisfying. The teacher Jos Thijssen is amazing and they cover super interesting topics. Mesoscopic physic is really great too and Herre van der Zant is an amazing teacher. Those two courses were the best that I took, really engaging, a bit difficult but really rewarding.

What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Amazing sports facilities with X at Delft. Also many social clubs. In the math department I joined the Christian Huygens study association

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Find a study association and join some sports. That is a great way to find friends with the same interests.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the nearby cities. Den Haag and Rotterdam are just nearby and super fun. Go to Amsterdam. Play a lot of sports at X.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Very similar do danish

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them in lectures. Do sports. Be open

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I dont know

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy your time there. Don't choose too many difficult courses. Enjoy your time and go to all social events.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get housing at DUWO.

questions.answer: Academics and friends I made
